title: GEPA
description: A framework for optimizing textual system components using LLM-based reflection and Pareto-efficient evolutionary search.

items.title: Named Failure Modes: Diagnosing the Program, Not Just the Output
items.content_html: A fully automatic second reviewer uses a learned guidebook of recurring process problems to improve GEPA by up to 9.7 percentage points under the same optimization budget.

items.title: Introducing the GEPA Blog
items.content_html: Research updates, applications, and community case studies from the GEPA ecosystem.

items.title: Automatically Learning Skills for Coding Agents
items.content_html: Introducing gskill, a fully automated pipeline that uses GEPA and SWE-smith to learn repository-specific skills for coding agents.

items.title: optimize_anything: A Universal API for Optimizing any Text Parameter
items.content_html: GEPA's new API setting state-of-the-art results on optimizing any text parameter: code, prompts, agent architectures, and more. If you can measure it, you can optimize it.

items.title: Confidence-Aware Prompt Optimization for LLM Classification
items.content_html: ConfidenceAdapter uses token-level log-probabilities to score prompt candidates on a continuous scale instead of binary correct/wrong, producing better disambiguation rules and higher-accuracy prompts for classification tasks.

items.title: Scaling GEPA with Combee: Parallel Prompt Learning for Self-Improving Agents
items.content_html: Exploring how to scale GEPA's prompt learning across many parallel agents using the Combee framework, achieving up to 17× speedup with no quality loss.

items.title: Learning, Fast and Slow: Towards LLMs That Adapt Continually
items.content_html: Fast-Slow Training (FST) interleaves prompt optimization with reinforcement learning, treating the prompt as fast weights and parameters as slow weights, improving data efficiency, performance ceiling, plasticity, and continual learning.

items.title: optimize_anything Goes omni: Composing Optimizers into Meta-Optimizer Pipelines
items.content_html: optimize_anything now supports customizable optimizers that can be composed into meta-optimizer pipelines. Why compose? Because no single optimizer wins everywhere. Our omni meta-optimizer combines the best of each and beats every standalone optimizer on Frontier-CS tasks under a matched budget.

items.title: Batching the Reflective Optimization Loop: Parallel Proposals Make GEPA Faster and Better
items.content_html: GEPA now supports proposing and evaluating a batch of candidates on each optimization step instead of one candidate at a time. In our sweep on two tasks, most batched runs finished in half the wall-clock time or less, and the fastest in about a quarter to a third. Batched settings also achieved higher held-out test scores: from 68.9% to 72.1% on LiveBench-Math (with 2×2) and from 49.0% to 60.0% on HoVer (with 8×1).
